verdict: AT&T grew revenue 5% and added over 1 million advanced-connectivity customers, but a $2.6B non-cash write-down of its Mexico business — which it has agreed to sell — cut GAAP EPS to $0.13 from $1.29.

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP)
kpis.note: from continuing operations, vs $1.29 a year ago (which included the DIRECTV sale gain); adjusted EPS was $0.65 vs $0.54

kpis.label: Postpaid phone net adds
kpis.note: plus a record 769,000 internet net adds (442,000 fiber, 327,000 fixed wireless)

kpis.label: Free cash flow
kpis.note: cash from operations of $10.5B minus $5.1B of capital spending and $0.5B of vendor financing

segments.name: Advanced Connectivity
segments.note: 5G wireless plus fiber internet for homes and businesses — service revenue rose 6.1%, with 379,000 postpaid phone net adds and a record 769,000 internet net adds.

segments.name: Legacy
segments.note: Old copper-network voice and data services, being shut down as customers move to fiber and 5G — revenue fell 24.5% on purpose.

segments.name: Latin America
segments.note: Wireless service and phones in Mexico — revenue rose 13.2% on postpaid growth and currency effects. AT&T agreed on Oct 13, 2026 to sell this business.

segments.name: Corporate & Other
segments.note: Small corporate and other revenues that do not belong to a segment — $82M vs $98M a year ago.

opex.name: SG&A
opex.note: Selling, support and head-office costs, including $44M of transaction, legal and other costs — higher equipment and bad-debt costs from subscriber growth, partly offset by cost-cutting.

opex.name: Impairments & restructuring
opex.note: Asset impairments, abandonments and restructuring — dominated by a $2.6B non-cash impairment of the Mexico wireless business AT&T has agreed to sell, plus employee separation charges.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: The wear-and-tear cost of the network and equipment — down 6.4% as old copper assets finish depreciating.

takeaways.title: Best service growth in four years
takeaways.text: Revenue rose 5.3% to $32.3B — the strongest consolidated service revenue growth in more than four years — as Advanced Connectivity service revenue grew 6.1% and its operating income jumped 18.9% to $7.6B.

takeaways.title: Mexico write-down sinks GAAP profit
takeaways.text: A $2.6B non-cash impairment on the Mexico wireless business (now held for sale) plus separation charges cut operating income to $4.1B from $6.1B. Adjusted operating income was $7.6B, up from $6.6B.

takeaways.title: Record internet additions
takeaways.text: AT&T added 769,000 fiber and fixed-wireless internet customers — a record — and 379,000 postpaid phones, passing 39 million fiber locations on the way to 40 million by year-end.

oneTimers: $2.6B non-cash impairment charge on the held-for-sale Mexico wireless business, inside the $3,372M impairments, abandonments and restructuring line.
Employee separation charges — together with the impairment and other items, adjustments total $0.52 per share (adjusted EPS $0.65 vs $0.13 GAAP).
Year-ago comparison is distorted the other way: Q3 2025 included a large gain on the sale of the DIRECTV investment in other income.
otherDetail: Other income of -$1,399M is $1,979M of interest expense, minus a $10M equity loss in affiliates, plus $590M of other income (mainly pension and interest income).
footerNote: This page models CONTINUING operations, as AT&T headlines them. The flow ends at net income attributable to common stock from continuing operations ($892M = $1,306M of continuing income, less $378M attributable to noncontrolling interests and $36M of preferred dividends). Including a $37M loss from discontinued operations (the held-for-sale Forged Fiber 37 business), total net income was $1,269M and net income attributable to common stock was $855M. AT&T realigned its segments in Q1 2026 — Advanced Connectivity, Legacy and Latin America replaced the old Communications structure — so segments here follow the new reporting.
